facts.text: Settled in 1659 and incorporated in 1812, Fairhaven grew around a bustling whaling harbor that still echoes its maritime past.
In 1841, author Herman Melville departed from Fairhaven’s port aboard the whaleship Acushnet, a launch point for his famous voyage.
Joshua Slocum, the first man to sail alone around the world, lived in Fairhaven and his ship Spray once rested in the town’s Poverty Point.
The Fairhaven Historical Society, founded in 1992, runs a museum that showcases an authentic early‑19th‑century classroom and other town artifacts.
Fairhaven High School, donated by Rogers in 1906, stands as a prominent landmark on Route 6 and has long been a community focal point.
Fairhaven shares its harbor with neighboring New Bedford, linking the two towns in a shared history of whaling and fishing.
